newsitem.title: USA: Freightliner to proceed with Ford truck purchase.
newsitem.headline: Freightliner to proceed with Ford truck purchase.

text.p: Freightliner Corp. said its bid to buy the heavy truck business of Ford Motor Co can move forward because the waiting period for the Hart-Scott-Rodino Act expired.

Freightliner, a leader in the North American heavy truck market, is a unit of German's Daimler-Benz AG. The company signed a definitive agreement in May to buy the technology, tooling and assembly equipment for Ford's heavy truck unit. Financial terms for the deal, first announced in February, have not been released.
"We are very pleased to be able to proceed with our transaction plans now," said Freighliner President and Chief Executive Officer James Hebe said.
"An announcement of the manufacturing sites for the products purchased from Ford and other details are planned for late June," he said.
Canadian authorities have also given their authorization for the deal to proceed, Hebe said.
The deal includes Ford's Louisville/AeroMax trucks, Ford's service parts business and all remaining tooling for the predecessor Ford L-Series trucks and the Ford Cargo truck.
